cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Ready on My Terms
cards.instruction: Agree to be honest, hopeful, or vulnerable only in forms that preserve your emotional safety.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I'll sit by the door while we talk about trying again. Please.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Knowing I can leave is helping me stay.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can stop when you need to.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I want to come home. Please don't hand me a key yet; saying it is enough for tonight.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 chooses a safe seat and A5 speaks hope with no-key boundary, but A3 authority assertion does not negotiate a concrete change with B.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 run concern follows door choice; B4 stopping permission can enable A5 home wish without committing to return immediately.

relationship.evidence: B2 worries A will leave and B4 offers flexible stopping to keep the conversation possible.

heightening.evidence: B4 safety offer causes A5 more vulnerable speech with a boundary on action.

specificity.evidence: A1 trying again and A5 coming home establish reconciliation; the exact prior rupture is unnecessary.
